text:
marta: FYI hit a weird race while onboarding the Go SDK generator streams. sample app shows stream.Next() hanging when token rotates mid-stream.

kai: can you share the minimal repro and sdk version?

marta: using go SDK v0.12.1. repro is tiny: 
```go
ctx := context.Background()
cli := redwood.NewClient(credentials)
stream, _ := cli.GenerateStream(ctx, opts)
for stream.Next() { fmt.Print(stream.Chunk().Text) }
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
```
Rotate creds externally after ~10s and the server returns unauth but the client never reconnects.

simon: is your code swapping client or updating headers? our streaming transport currently sets auth at dial time.

marta: we rotate the token via a background refresh and swap the client instance. but existing stream stays open and fails. the app has no timeout, so it fogs the customer experience.

kai: hmm. short-term workaround: cancel the ctx and re-create the stream on refresh. long-term we should support transparent reauth.

aaron: Proposal: add an AuthHook to generator options. ergonomic API:
```go
type AuthHook func(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
opts.WithAuthHook(myHook)
```
SDK calls AuthHook on reconnect attempts and before each rpc if transport supports it.

simon: agree. also need sample app demonstrating auth-hook + backoff + resume. add it to sdk/go/samples/ so users see the pattern.

marta: i can draft the sample and a tiny test that simulates a 401 mid-stream and asserts client recovers. will open a PR.

ci-bot: CI: run/sdk-go-e2e #221 queued

kai: one more thought 94 make sure we document signal handling (ctx cancellation) vs auth refresh. lots of users cancel context which makes it ambiguous in bug reports. quickstart blurb should call out that rotating creds need either AuthHook or ctx lifecycle management.

aaron: noted. i'll take the quickstart copy update after the PR lands.

marta: thanks all. i'll post PR link when ready.
